title: Setup Instructions for Students
text:
Follow these steps to set up and publish your research website.


Before you begin, make sure you have the following:

A GitHub account (free at github.com)
GitHub Desktop installed on your computer
R and RStudio







Click the “Use this template” button.
Select Create a new repository.
Use the Owner dropdown menu to select your github user
Name the repository. This will be in your web address! Choose something professional like your name.
Click Create repository from template.
You should now have this newly created repository on your own GitHub.





On your computer: Make sure the GitHub Desktop is open.
On GitHub: In your own repository on GitHub, Click the “<> Code” button.
Select Open with GitHub Desktop.
Choose a local path for the placement of the directory (not a cloud service). For example: (/Users/YourUserame/GitHub/introR2026)
Select Clone.





[!IMPORTANT] 1. Open RStudio 2. Create a new Rproj file in the existing local directory of your repository 3. Open .Rproj file 4. Edit the following files in RStudio




Replace “Your Name” with your name.
Update the About Me section.
Add your research interests.
Replace “your photo.jpg” with the filename of a photo of yourself & by adding the photo to the directory.
Update places that say “link” with the correct internet link or email address, if desired.





Update the descriptions of your projects.
Add links to additional projects as you create them.





Change the title to your project title.
Write your final report.
Replace all placeholder text with your own content.




styles.css * Customize colors, fonts, and other styling options if desired.
_quarto.yml * add new links to the navbar
README.md * This is a place to add information to the GitHub reponsitory, but will not be displayed on your rendered website.
.gitignore * List files here you don’t want synced to GitHub. For example, if you want to keep your data.csv files local and not online list them here
SETUP.md * These are instructions to create this site. No need to modify this file.




In RStudio, you can preview your website before publishing.
Run the following command in the RStudio Terminal:
quarto preview
To render the website before pushing your changes, run:
quarto render



When you are satisfied with your changes:

Open GitHub Desktop.
Review the files you modified.
Enter a commit summary and an optional description.
Click Commit to main.
Click Push origin to upload your changes to GitHub.





Go to your repository on GitHub.
Click Settings.
Select Pages from the left sidebar.
Under Build and deployment:

Source: Select Deploy from a branch.
Branch: Select main.
Folder: Select /docs.

Click Save.





Wait 1–2 minutes for GitHub to deploy your site.
Return to Settings → Pages.
You should see a URL similar to:
https://YOUR-USERNAME.github.io/YOUR-REPOSITORY/
Click the link to view your website.





Whenever you want to update your website:

Edit your .qmd files.
Commit and push your changes using GitHub Desktop.
Wait 1–2 minutes for GitHub Pages to rebuild your site.
Refresh your browser to view the updated website.




If your website is not updating:

Go to your GitHub repository.
Click the Actions tab.
Open the most recent workflow run.
Review any error messages if the build failed.







Go to Settings → Pages.
Confirm that:

The branch is set to main.
The folder is set to /docs.

Your website URL should appear on this page after deployment.




Always use forward slashes (/) in links, even when using Windows.
# Correct
[Link](projects/final-report.qmd)

# Incorrect
[Link](projects\final-report.qmd)




To add another page, such as a poster, publication, or additional project:

Create a new .qmd file in the projects/ folder.
Edit projects.qmd and add a link to the new page.
Commit and push your changes.
Wait 1–2 minutes for GitHub Pages to update your website.





Quarto Documentation
GitHub Pages Documentation
Markdown Guide
Git Basics


Need help? Contact your instructor or refer to the resources listed above.

title: Final Report: Sleep Quality and Lifestyle Analysis
text:
Sleeping is a biological phenomenon that helps in the maintenance of health, cognition, emotions, and general wellness. Adequate sleep time and good sleep quality are important determinants of quality of life and well-being. Several studies have indicated that psychological stress has an impact on sleep patterns by decreasing the quality of sleep and sleep duration. Moreover, physical activity has been known to have a role in the regulation of sleep through improving the quality of sleep and the general well-being. The influence of stress levels and physical activity on the quality of sleep may be different among individuals depending on lifestyle and demographics like gender.

#Data work flow
## =========================================================
## Question 1: Does physical activity affect sleep?
## =========================================================
## Easy method: split people into "Low" vs "High" activity groups
## using the median, then just compare the average sleep quality
## and duration between the two groups.

sleep = sleep |>
  mutate(activity_group = if_else(physical_activity_level >= median(physical_activity_level),
                                   "High Activity", "Low Activity"))


## Plot: average sleep quality by activity group
ggplot(sleep,
    aes(x = activity_group,
         y = quality_of_sleep,
         fill = activity_group)) +
geom_boxplot() +
stat_compare_means(
method = "t.test",
label = "p.signif"
   ) +
 labs(
        title = "Sleep Quality by Physical Activity Group",
         x = "Activity Group",
         y = "Sleep Quality (1-10)"
     ) +
     theme_minimal()







## Plot: average sleep duration by activity group
ggplot(sleep,
    aes(x = activity_group,
         y = sleep_duration,
         fill = activity_group)) +
geom_boxplot() +
stat_compare_means(
method = "t.test",
label = "p.signif"
   ) +
 labs(
        title = "Sleep Duration by Physical Activity Group",
         x = "Activity Group",
         y = "Sleep Quality (1-10)"
     ) +
     theme_minimal()







# =========================================================
## Question 2: Do daily steps affect sleep?
## =========================================================
## Same easy method: split into "Low Steps" vs "High Steps" using median
sleep = sleep |>
  mutate(steps_group = if_else(daily_steps >= median(daily_steps),
                                   "Higher daily steps", "Lower daily steps"))
## Plot: average sleep quality by steps group
ggplot(sleep,
    aes(x = steps_group,
         y = quality_of_sleep,
         fill = steps_group)) +
geom_boxplot() +
stat_compare_means(
method = "t.test",
label = "p.signif"
   ) +
 labs(
        title = "Sleep Quality by Daily steps Group",
         x = "Activity Group",
         y = "Sleep Quality (1-10)"
     ) +
     theme_minimal()







## Plot: average sleep duration by steps group
ggplot(sleep,
    aes(x = steps_group,
         y = sleep_duration,
         fill = steps_group)) +
geom_boxplot() +
stat_compare_means(
method = "t.test",
label = "p.signif"
   ) +
 labs(
        title = "Sleep Duration by Daily step Group",
         x = "Activity Group",
         y = "Sleep Quality (1-10)"
     ) +
     theme_minimal()

## Question 2: Do daily steps affect sleep?
## =========================================================
## Same easy method: split into "Low Steps" vs "High Steps" using median
sleep = sleep |>
  mutate(steps_group = if_else(daily_steps >= median(daily_steps),
                                   "Higher daily steps", "Lower daily steps"))
## Plot: average sleep quality by steps group
ggplot(sleep,
    aes(x = steps_group,
         y = quality_of_sleep,
         fill = steps_group)) +
geom_boxplot() +
stat_compare_means(
method = "t.test",
label = "p.signif"
   ) +
 labs(
        title = "Sleep Quality by Daily steps Group",
         x = "Activity Group",
         y = "Sleep Quality (1-10)"
     ) +
     theme_minimal()







## Plot: average sleep duration by steps group
ggplot(sleep,
    aes(x = steps_group,
         y = sleep_duration,
         fill = steps_group)) +
geom_boxplot() +
stat_compare_means(
method = "t.test",
label = "p.signif"
   ) +
 labs(
        title = "Sleep Duration by Daily step Group",
         x = "Activity Group",
         y = "Sleep Quality (1-10)"
     ) +
     theme_minimal()







# =========================================================
## Question 3: Does stress level affect sleep?
## =========================================================
#A correlation analysis showed that stress level was strongly associated with sleep quality. Participants with higher stress levels tended to report poorer sleep quality (r = -0.90, p < 0.001).

Here are my research projects and work:


My final project for CELL 6351 - Intro to Reproducible Data Analysis Using R. Sleeping is a biological phenomenon that helps in the maintenance of health, cognition, emotions, and general wellness. Adequate sleep time and good sleep quality are important determinants of quality of life and well-being. Several studies have indicated that psychological stress has an impact on sleep patterns by decreasing the quality of sleep and sleep duration. Moreover, physical activity has been known to have a role in the regulation of sleep through improving the quality of sleep and the general well-being. The influence of stress levels and physical activity on the quality of sleep may be different among individuals depending on lifestyle and demographics like gender.
